transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-09-10
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Sam Rivera (Horizon Head of ML), Maya Patel (Eng Lead), Tom Diaz (CTO), Ravi (Data Eng)

Summary:
Horizon is evaluating options for embeddings + reranking for their semantic search and recommendation pipelines. Primary concerns: throughput (QPS), vector dimensionality tradeoffs, hybrid search with keyword filters, VPC/private deployment for regulated data, and cost comparisons between hosted and dedicated options. They want a short POC to measure latency and recall vs their current FAISS-based infra.

Topics Covered:
- vector DB integrations (Pinecone/Qdrant/Weaviate/FAISS)
- embeddings dimensionality and model choices (open vs provider models)
- throughput and batching for production QPS
- hybrid search (keyword + vector rerank)
- security: VPC, KMS, SOC2, data residency
- POC scope and next steps

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um I'm Alex from Redwood, and with me is Priya our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Sam: Good, thanks. Busy week but excited to get into this. We've got a lot riding on search improvements so we wanna see how Redwood fits.
[00:15] Maya: quick note, Tom's gotta jump at 15:30 but he wanted to hear the architecture bits.
[00:20] Alex: got it, we'll try to cover the high-level first then dive infra. Priya, you wanna kick off with how we usually do embeddings + rerank?
[00:28] Priya: yeah sure. So at a high level, teams use us for embeddings generation and then either store vectors in your vector DB of choice or use our hosted index. For reranking we typically do a two-stage flow: first a vector retrieval for recall, then a lightweight reranker model or asymmetric cross-encoder to reorder results. We support streaming, batching and can route to Hosted, Dedicated GPU pools, or Private VPC deployments.
[00:50] Sam: quick Q — we currently run FAISS on prem with 768-d embeddings. Our QPS is around 400 reads/sec at peak, 120 writes per minute. We need sub-50ms tail latency for the first-stage retrieval. Can Redwood hit that?
[01:05] Priya: depends on deployment. For Hosted endpoints hitting sub-50ms per-query for a 10–20 nearest neighbor search is tough at 400 QPS without batching or a dedicated pool. Our Dedicated nodes with pinned GPUs and optimized ANN engines get us there, especially if you pipelined with caching for hot queries. Also hybrid search on the vector DB side can help you keep latency down — e.g., use an index with HNSW + product quantization on the vectors and offload some filtering to the DB layer.
[01:35] Maya: we use a lot of metadata filters — tenant_id, region, document_type — we need hybrid filtering. Do you have recommended vector DBs?
[01:42] Priya: commonly customers use Pinecone and Qdrant, also Milvus internally. Weaviate has nice schema filtering too. If you want to keep everything in-house, FAISS can be good but it becomes operationally heavy at scale. We can integrate with your existing DB; or for dedicated/private we can bundle the vector index inside the private deployment.
[02:00] Tom: question — dimensionality. We currently use 768-d, but saw some teams go up to 1536 or down to 256. What's Redwood's guidance?
[02:08] Alex: generally higher dims can improve recall but cost more in storage and compute. Our recommendations: run a small eval across your critical query set — measure recall vs latency and storage. For many customers 768 or 1024 hits a good balance. Priya, we have notes about quantized models and 8-bit embeddings?
[02:23] Priya: yeah you can quantize vectors (PQ) to reduce memory; also we recommend trying a larger base model and then reducing dim via PCA/OPQ if you need stable lower dims. For reranking using a cross-encoder you can keep small dims and rely on an expensive re-rank for the top-k.
[02:38] Ravi: on storage — if we keep vectors in S3 plus a shard index, any recommendations on warm-up times for cold queries?
[02:45] Priya: cold starts vary. If using Dedicated GPU pools with warmed-up indices, warm-up is negligible. If you spin up nodes dynamically, there is startup time. Our cache layer can keep hot prefixes in memory to reduce that.
[02:58] Sam: security is huge for us — we need VPC peering, BYOK KMS, and audit logs. Do you support on-prem private control plane?
[03:08] Alex: yes — our Private offering supports customer VPCs, optional on-prem packages, and KMS/HSM integrations for key management. We can provide audit logs and long retention as an add-on. We'll send SOC2 and ISO docs after this call.
[03:20] Maya: curious about throughput numbers — you said Dedicated pools can handle 400 QPS, do you have example metrics?
[03:27] Priya: I can share ballpark — on a p4-like instance with optimized ANN we can serve ~500 small vector queries/sec with ~20–40ms p95 for 768-d when batch size and indexing are tuned. Embedding generation throughput depends on model size; for an LLM-based embedder we can do ~120–300 requests/sec per GPU depending on batching and sequence length.
[03:51] Tom: what about cost tradeoffs? Hosted per-token/embedding pricing vs reserved Dedicated?
[03:58] Alex: Hosted is simpler, pay-as-you-go; Dedicated is reserved capacity with better unit economics at scale and SLA guarantees. For predictable 24/7 throughput, Dedicated usually wins. For bursts or early evals Hosted is easier. We can show a TCO worksheet — we'll include in follow-up.
[04:15] Sam: for reranking, do you recommend doing a cross-encoder on the fly or precompute some features? Latency will be sensitive.
[04:22] Priya: common pattern: retrieval with vector store (fast), then re-rank top-10 with a cross-encoder. The re-ranker can be a smaller model to cut latency. You can also precompute asymmetric features or use sparse keyword overlap to reduce re-ranker calls. Hybrid search combining BM25 + vector recall often reduces the number of expensive re-rank ops.
[04:45] Maya: integration — how do we connect our vector DB? Any connectors or SDKs?
[04:50] Priya: we have SDKs and REST endpoints. For Pinecone/Qdrant/Milvus we have examples; for FAISS we provide guidance and a reference deploy. If you want Redwood-managed index, we expose API and we'll handle scaling.
[05:02] Sam: during a POC we'd want to run our 5k query benchmark and see recall/latency and cost per query. How do we set that up?
[05:10] Alex: next step would be to run a scoped POC: you provide sample dataset and query set (5k), we give sandbox credentials (Hosted or Dedicated sandbox), run baseline with your FAISS setup and our flows, and produce a comparison doc. Priya will own the bench plan.
[05:25] Priya: I'll draft a benchmark plan — we'll need sample vectors, queries, expected metrics (p95 latency, recall@k), and budget/acceptable windows. Also need to know whether you'll allow us to spin up a dedicated pool for the test or use hosted endpoints.
[05:40] Maya: probably hosted first, but if latency is off we'll switch to a dedicated sandbox.
[05:45] Tom: small nit — do you support hybrid retrieval in a single query? Meaning keyword filters + vector similarity in one step rather than separate client joins.
[05:53] Priya: yes, some vector DBs support filter predicates natively (Pinecone/Weaviate). For others you can apply metadata filters at query-time and then run vector retrieval. Our SDK helps orchestrate that so it's effectively a single call from your app.
[06:07] Ravi: about dimensionality again — any recommended models? Open models vs Redwood-verified models?
[06:13] Alex: we have a catalog. For embeddings many customers pick open models like the small OpenAI-style open-source models or our Redwood-verified models tuned for embeddings. We'll attach a short matrix with accuracy vs cost vs dim.
[06:25] Sam: latency SLA — if we go Dedicated with reserved capacity, do you offer SLOs on p95?
[06:31] Alex: yes, Dedicated comes with uptime and latency targets depending on commit tier. We'll include SLA language in the contract.
[06:36] Maya: network setup — if we do Private in our VPC, what's the control plane look like?
[06:41] Priya: Private gives you a control plane that can be hosted in your VPC or as an air-gapped on-prem bundle. You manage networking; we provide orchestration and observability agents. KMS integration is via standard key wrap/APIs. We'll share the architecture doc.
[06:56] Sam: any customers in regulated industries doing this?
[07:00] Alex: yes, finance and healthcare customers use Private with long retention logs and HSMs. We'll connect you with a reference.
[07:07] Tom: about rerank models — are they hosted as part of Redwood runtime or do we bring our own model?
[07:12] Priya: both. You can bring your own reranker (we'll serve it) or use Redwood-managed rerankers. We support common frameworks and containerized models.
[07:21] Sam: ok, let's talk success criteria for POC — what would make this a win for Horizon?
[07:27] Maya: improvement in recall@10 by +8–10% over FAISS baseline, p95 retrieval latency under 80ms for first-stage, and cost per query under our current $0.0009 target. Also must prove VPC/TLS + KMS meets our security bar.
[07:41] Alex: great, that's actionable. We'll draft the POC scope and include these as acceptance criteria.
[07:47] Priya: I'll schedule the benchmark and need a couple of things: sample dataset, queries, and whether you'll allow a dedicated sandbox.
[07:55] Sam: we can provision S3 access for you to pull the samples.
[07:59] Maya: I'll create a share and ping Priya offline.
[08:03] Tom: I gotta jump — appreciate the overview. Please send the security docs and pricing.
[08:08] Tom: (leaves)
[08:10] Alex: thanks Tom. Before we go deeper, any other architecture questions?
[08:14] Maya: one more — for large-scale writes, do you recommend bulk ingest pipelines or streaming? We ingest 50k docs/day, sometimes spiky loads up to 200k/day.
[08:23] Priya: bulk ingest with batched embeddings tends to be cheaper. For spikes, pipelines that write to S3 and then batch process into the vector index work well. We can also support streaming ingestion into Dedicated pools with autoscaling bursts.
[08:36] Ravi: curious about index maintenance — reindex frequency for updated docs?
[08:40] Priya: depends on update rate. For frequent small updates, append/partial updates are fine; for global schema changes full reindex is recommended. We'll share best practices doc.
[08:50] Sam: what about observability — can we get token-level cost breakdowns and per-route dashboards?
[08:56] Alex: yes that's Redwood Console — you get token-level (for generation) and per-route latency/cost, plus traces and error analysis. We'll include screenshots in follow-up.
[09:06] Maya: excellent. On pricing, we'd like a TCO with hosted vs dedicated 3- and 12-month views.
[09:12] Alex: will do. Anything else?
[09:15] Sam: no, thanks this was helpful. We'll expect the benchmark plan and security docs.
[09:20] Alex: recap of next steps: Alex will send pricing + security docs; Priya will draft benchmark plan and coordinate sandbox; Maya will share sample dataset; schedule technical deep dive next week for SE-led performance optimization.
[09:34] Maya: thanks everyone. Bye.
